paper.title: Self-Modification of Policy and Utility Function in Rational Agents
paper.central_claim: Depending on how expected utility is optimised (hedonistic, ignorant, realistic value functions), a rational agent that can self-modify its policy or utility function will either modify itself harmfully or, if realistic (current utility judges the future with self-modification anticipated), will not make harmful modifications (Theorem 16).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: subagent runtime exposes no receipt to the worker; model identity is the configured claude-kimi type only. Pure theory paper read through Section 6 and Appendix A (theorem statements and proof sketches); scope exclusion.

evidence.quote: We define formal models for two general kinds of self-modifications, where the agent can either change its future policy or its future utility function.
evidence.support_explanation: The paper models self-modification abstractly (policy or utility function swapped by an action); no concrete non-weight component, execution feedback, or retention loop.

evidence.quote: We approached this question from the perspective of rationality and utility maximisation, which abstracts away from most details of architecture and implementation.
Our main result Theorem 16 shows that it is possible to create an agent that despite being able to make any self-modification will refrain from using it.
evidence.support_explanation: Main result is about agents that refrain from self-modification (safety), not about improving components from feedback.

evidence.quote: we want that things cannot go wrong rather than things can go right
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state the safety orientation of the result.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we assumed that the agent knew the self-modifying consequences of its actions.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-modification consequences are given, not learned from execution feedback.

Searched all sections and Appendix A: no implementation, benchmark, experiment, executable component, feedback-driven edit or measurement of any later-task gain exists; results are theorems about optimal policies under three value-function definitions.

status_reason: Scope (docs/EVIDENCE.md, SCORE_SPEC): requires a system that changes and retains non-weight components from execution feedback. This paper is an architecture-free theory of when an idealised rational agent would choose to self-modify its policy/utility; there is no execution feedback, concrete component, retained change or evidence of later improvement, and the main theorem is about abstaining from self-modification. Scope question for control: the domain card H31 (evidence_gated_retention) lists theory members of this kind, so control may decide to admit theory-only commit-rule papers under a new claim_type.
